subject.title: RFC: OpenShell session workers and local inference

question: Should OpenClaw make provider-authenticated worker transport and immutable worker-local inference permanent generic core contracts for plugin-provisioned workers?
rationale: The RFC deliberately adds protocol, persistence, transport, provider-routing, and credential-boundary surface; tests cannot determine whether this is the desired permanent architecture.

options.title: Review The Narrow Contract
options.body: Continue the RFC with live proof and security and upgrade review while keeping OpenShell policy plugin-owned and Gateway-proxy inference as the default.

options.title: Provision Workers Only
options.body: Accept OpenShell as a worker provider but defer worker-local inference and its provider-routing contract.

options.title: Retain Current Boundaries
options.body: Decline the new core seams and keep OpenShell limited to its existing tool-sandbox role.

recommendation.title: Review The Narrow Contract
recommendation.body: Continue the RFC with live proof and security and upgrade review while keeping OpenShell policy plugin-owned and Gateway-proxy inference as the default.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the best available routing candidate for an RFC-level permanent core architecture decision, while sallyom remains the technical integration owner.
